subject.title: Stale client registration replayed to DCR forever; only --reset recovers

question: Should a changed MCP server configuration or a rejected cached DCR registration automatically clear client information and retry once, and which DCR errors are safe to classify as stale rather than transient?
rationale: The code change is likely small, but choosing an error-classification and invalidation policy affects stored OAuth state, provider load, and recovery behavior beyond a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Define a narrow stale-DCR retry
options.body: Invalidate cached client information only for an explicit server-identity change or a provider error contract that proves the registration is invalid, then retry registration once.

options.title: Keep reset-only recovery
options.body: Retain the current manual reset behavior until providers expose a sufficiently reliable stale-registration signal.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow stale-DCR retry
recommendation.body: Invalidate cached client information only for an explicit server-identity change or a provider error contract that proves the registration is invalid, then retry registration once.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior merged OAuth recovery work is the closest available history for the intended invalidation policy.
